cand.title: Paléo Festival 2027
cand.excerpt: High repeat-demand potential and local relevance; current accessibility requires careful role definition.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Dany Hassenstein, Responsable Artistes et Scènes, is the strongest identified operational approach: his July 2026 interview explicitly includes “les transports, les hôtels” among artist negotiations and says 2027 discussions had already begun. Daniel Rossellat, president of Paléo Arts & Spectacles and festival leader, is a verified strategic escalation contact. Neither is verified as the sole hotel-contract signatory. Use the association’s published general business channel to request routing to the actual accommodation purchaser.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced: 19–25 July 2027, Nyon, Vaud, Switzerland. The official homepage states: “See you from 19 to 25 July 2027 for the next edition of Paléo!” and “To celebrate its 50th anniversary, the Festival will exceptionally take place over 7 days.” These are activity dates, within the requested horizon; not article dates. No exact 2028 festival dates were established.
findings.hotelProductFit: Commercial inference using the supplied hotel brief: YOTEL Geneva Lake is a plausible off-site base for a limited artist-entourage, production/project-team or partner group, not the festival venue or housing solution for the entire audience. Its Founex/La Côte location is relevant to Nyon rather than downtown Geneva. Explore a phased 20–120-room proposal only as the hotel’s commercial band, never as published event demand or available inventory. Hotel meeting/F&B areas could support small briefings or team meals, not festival performances or mass plenaries. Transport is decisive: the regional tourism page places the hotel about 12 minutes by car from Nyon station, and Paléo publishes a Nyon–L’Asse rail connection; neither proves a hotel shuttle or 2027 late-night door-to-door access. This is not a resort-retreat event.
findings.venueCommitments: Venue: Plaine de l’Asse, Nyon area, Canton of Vaud, Switzerland — Nyon/La Côte territory, not Founex itself, Geneva city or Lausanne. Official venue wording: “The destination is the now iconic ‘Plaine de l’Asse’ in Nyon.” The announced 2027 edition and fixed-site history support continued use of this site; a separate edition-specific signed site agreement was not published in the sources reviewed. Route de St-Cergue 312 is the organizer’s contact address and must not replace the named festival grounds. This is an outdoor festival venue, not a competing hotel.
findings.historicalRotation: Not a destination-rotation opportunity: the official chronology records an indoor Nyon beginning in 1976, Colovray from 1977 through 1989, then the move to Plaine de l’Asse in 1990. Recent editions: 23–28 July 2024; 22–27 July 2025; 21–26 July 2026, at the established Nyon site. A proposed historical Vich move did not become an edition. Recurrence is verified by successive editions, not merely an inferred annual pattern.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Hotel sourcing remains unconfirmed. Official lodging quote: “In addition to the traditional free campsite, the Festival offers the Camping Pal’Asse (for a fee), as well as a campervan zone with improved services.” No hotels are named on this official lodging page; no official housing bureau, hotel host, published hotel block or open hotel RFP was identified. Thus the complete verified official hotel-name list is empty, not a claim that no private hotel contracts exist. Pal’Asse is glamping operated by Lodg’ing, not a hotel bureau. Lodg’ing markets 18–26 July 2027 packages and says “Nos tarifs 2027: à venir”; its partnership text still says “s’associent en 2026”. The official Sleep page retains 20–27 July camping dates and seven-day sold-out wording: these must not be presented as 2027 hotel commitments or availability.
findings.organizationStructure: Event owner/organizer: Paléo Arts et Spectacles (also styled Paléo Arts & Spectacles), an independent non-profit association, not a corporate conference owner or a PCO/DMC. The association is the strategic body; the Comité d’Organisation du Festival handles operations, and major decisions are collegial. Lodg’ing is the named consumer glamping operator, not the event owner or a verified hotel buyer. No separate external hotel-procurement agency was established.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Public on-site camping and paid Pal’Asse glamping are established alternatives to hotel stays. The 2026 closing release reports 250,000 festivalgoers, 8,000 campers and more than 1,000 campervans; these are historical festival/camping figures, not unique overnight hotel customers, peak rooms or room-nights. Lodg’ing is a named incumbent in glamping, but no hotel incumbent or exclusive hotel arrangement was verified. There is no sourced hotel sell-out or overflow evidence; do not claim displaced demand. High festival attendance does not establish hotel conversion.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Dany Hassenstein through Paléo Arts et Spectacles at info@paleo.ch / +41 22 365 10 10. Request the named artist/production accommodation purchaser and a short supplier-qualification call: which cohorts need off-site hotels, who contracts/pays, incumbent hotels/bureau, release dates, stay pattern and room mix, realistic nightly peak, transport and late check-in requirements, and any unmet 2027 allocations. Present a conditional phased 20–120-room hotel proposal with transport priced separately; do not reserve the whole 237-room house or quote against assumed demand. Use Daniel Rossellat’s office only for strategic routing. If contracted, ask when future-cycle hotel suppliers are reviewed.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the next announced edition, 2027, dates are confirmed but hotel procurement accessibility is unknown: no public accommodation tender or unallocated hotel block was found. Artist negotiations for 2027 were already underway by July 2026; this supports approaching the production pathway now, not claiming that hotel buying remains open. Public camping/glamping availability is separate from organizer-paid lodging. Existing private hotel commitments may exist and must be established directly.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeated editions at the Nyon site make an accommodation-supplier relationship commercially more plausible than bidding to relocate the festival to the hotel. If 2027 lodging is committed, seek supplier onboarding and permission to quote the next uncontracted cycle. An interview mentions an artist negotiation for 2028, but this is not a published 2028 festival date or a hotel-sourcing window. A permanent-staff vacancy covers collaborator welfare from four weeks before to three weeks after the festival; this supports asking about project-team needs, not claiming seven weeks of paid hotel demand.
